title: Dedicated Capacity: Guardrail Autoscale + Tenant Sandbox PRD
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This PRD defines a new Dedicated capacity feature set that introduces: 1) Guardrail Autoscale: predictive autoscaling with conservative burst caps and safety preemption to protect reserved customers; 2) Tenant Sandbox pools: ephemeral, low-latency isolated prewarm pools for high-variance tenants that allow temporary burst capacity without degrading reservation SLAs; and 3) Transparent attribution and soft-fallback rules that ensure predictable billing and graceful degradation.
goals: Prevent noisy bursts from causing SLA regressions for reservation customers
Allow bursty tenants to achieve short-term throughput without long-term overprovisioning
Keep end-to-end token latency within configured SLOs during mixed workloads
Provide clear billing attribution for sandbox usage and autoscale actions
Make guardrail behavior auditable and configurable by tenant and admin
non_goals: Rearchitecting the serving runtime kernel selection (out of scope for this work)
Replacing existing global prewarm mechanisms for dedicated pools
Implementing per-request cost optimization heuristics beyond attribution
scope_in: Autoscale controller with conservative burst cap and lookahead prediction (short horizon)
Tenant Sandbox: ephemeral VM/GPU pools that can be spun up to a configurable cap and evicted first under pressure
API and Console controls: enable/disable sandbox, set per-tenant burst caps, configure guardrail strictness
Billing tags and dashboarding for sandbox/autoscale events
Acceptance test harness and SLO stress tests in staging
scope_out: Changes to Dedicated capacity contract/legal terms (billing model changes require legal review separate EPIC)
Extensive ML model-inference optimizations (e.g., quantization changes)
Cross-region live migration of active KV caches
success_metrics: <10% of surge incidents cause SLA breaches for reserved tenants (measured weekly)
Avg cost delta for tenants using sandbox < +15% compared to baseline expected for bursty workloads
95th percentile tail latency for reserved traffic remains within 1.2x of baseline under simulated bursts
Dashboard adoption: >80% of Dedicated customers can see sandbox attribution in Console within 1 week of rollout
acceptance_criteria: Feature flags exist to toggle Guardrail Autoscale and Tenant Sandbox independently
Autoscaler respects configured tenant caps and global safety quotas in the presence of concurrent spin-ups
Sandbox pools are created with tenant-scoped network/metadata and are the first candidates for preemption under system pressure
Billing events for sandbox/autoscale actions emit consistent tags enabling per-tenant cost reconciliation in billing pipeline
End-to-end integration test: synthetic mixed workload where 5 bursty tenants use sandbox and 3 reserved customers maintain SLOs; reserved SLOs are not violated
Console shows a timeline view of autoscale/sandbox events with links to incident traces
Rollout can be limited to a subset of accounts (whitelist) and disabled globally within a single toggle
Latency and error-rate regression thresholds set and enforced by CI gating for staging->prod promotion
privacy_and_compliance: Sandbox pools must obey customer data residency settings (no cross-region allocation unless tenant permits)
Audit logs for sandbox creation/deletion and autoscale decisions retained for 90 days by default
Security review required for any tenant-side scripts executed during sandbox provisioning
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sandboxes could be abused to bypass reservation limits -> Mitigation: per-tenant caps, rate-limited sandbox creation, audit alerts
Risk: Autoscale oscillation causing flapping -> Mitigation: conservative cooldowns, smoothing window, and max-change-per-minute limits
Risk: Unexpected billing spikes -> Mitigation: realtime billing alerts, spend thresholds that auto-disable sandbox, and manual approval flow for high caps
Risk: Increased operational complexity for SRE -> Mitigation: observability runbooks, default safe presets, and playbook training
dependencies: Provisioning API v2 (ENG-51234) for fast pool spin-up
Billing tagging pipeline change (BILL-2019) to accept sandbox/autoscale tags
Console timeline component (DES-98120) for event visualization
SLO simulation harness (ENG-48712) for validation tests
open_questions: What is the default sandbox cap per tenant for paid vs trial accounts?
Should sandbox usage be billed at a premium rate or discounted burst rate?
How many concurrent sandboxes can a single physical host support before we consider fragmentation?
Do we expose guardrail strictness as numeric E2E setting or named presets (conservative/standard/aggressive)?
design_notes: Prefer first-class tenant metadata on sandbox resources for clear attribution
Autoscaler should operate on an application-level token metric in addition to GPU utilization
Guardrails are policy-first; default policy must be conservative to protect legacy reserved SLAs
Expose a dry-run mode that surfaces what autoscale decisions would have been for 72 hours before enforcement
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike, 3w): Prototype autoscale lookahead and sandbox provisioning prototype in staging
Phase 2 (MVP, 6w): Implement autoscale controller, sandbox lifecycle, billing tags, limited-console controls, integration tests
Phase 3 (Rollout, 4w): Whitelist early customers, collect feedback, iterate on presets and default caps
Phase 4 (GA, 2w): Expand rollout, update docs, runbook, and enable alerts
rollout_plan: Start with internal accounts + 2 power customers as canaries
Enable feature flag on a per-account basis from Console and via API
Monitor reserved SLA metrics and billing telemetry closely for first 48 hours after enabling per-account
Gradually expand whitelist while adjusting default caps based on observed behavior
observability: Instrument autoscale decisions with decision reason codes and correlation IDs
Create dedicated dashboard: sandbox utilization, preemption count, reserved SLO impact, billing delta
Set automated alerts for preemption spikes and sandbox-related cost anomalies
notes_and_history: 2026-03-10: Initial PRD drafted by Aisha Kapoor. Focus: safe burst support without SLA regression.
2026-03-12: Engineering spike recommended tenant-scoped preemption as safest default (Priya Malhotra)
2026-03-14: Console team requested timeline visualization requirement to aid billing disputes (Dana Park)
Trade-offs discussed: aggressive autoscale would improve UX for bursty customers but increases risk to reserved SLAs; default conservative policy chosen.
